headline: Medium risk: shared document-processing and browser-based workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and output-cascade exposure; no direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and process documents/images, while pdf.js also runs browsers and consumes PDF files. A shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge is not documented, but if outputs from one are fed into the other, document content can carry instructions. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or clipboard, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent treats extracted document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate input/output folders per agent.
Disable copy-paste handoff between agents.
Require a human review step before any instruction-like text is acted on.
Strip executable-looking directives from OCR/PDF text before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and handles documents/images; pdf.js has no network egress and reads PDF files. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage is not established. If a shared directory exists, the blast radius is limited to document contents, making low the best fit.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same workspace, document contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content to an external API, document text may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Confirm PaddleOCR API calls are restricted to approved endpoints.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in any shared directory.
Run a quick audit of outbound requests during a test document.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR exposes API calls and browser execution, while pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests. The profiles do not show overlapping write access, git state, or shared mutable resources, so direct conflict is not proven. If both are pointed at the same writable directory, contention is possible but likely limited.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent runs may overwrite intermediate artifacts.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Keep one agent read-only when the other is writing.
Check for filename collisions before batch runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-parsing outputs that pdf.js could plausibly consume in browser-based tests or rendering workflows. The profiles do not document verification gates between them, so if pdf.js treats PaddleOCR output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream work. Because the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes OCR output without validation, transcription errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts extracted text as ground truth, incorrect actions may follow.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before reuse of OCR output.
Compare extracted text against the source PDF for a sample set.
Mark OCR-derived fields as untrusted metadata.
Require human approval before any action based on extracted text.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document-processing tools with no requested OAuth scopes or secrets, and no residency or certification mismatch is documented. The main compliance concern is document handling itself, not a specific regulatory conflict. Because no cross-border or PHI pathway is shown, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents such as PHI or EU PII are processed, policy review is required.
IF deployment adds retention or logging beyond the profiles, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Classify document types before processing.
Disable unnecessary logging of document contents.
Keep retention settings documented and minimal.
Review whether regulated data is allowed in the chosen deployment.
